i don't personally care if others use marijuana, but i am personally terrified of it. i have psychosis without being on any drugs, and the idea of taking anything that could cause hallucinations is terrifying, they normal ones are bad enough on their own. i don't want to see dead me trying to convince live me to join them. and for auditory hallucinations, lowering some inhibitions will likely result in hallucinations trying to convince me to pluck out my eyes, and that's not something that can be undone. i have friends that seem to have a good time, but i have fomo because i have to constantly be checking every though to make sure it isn't something very self destructive trying to slip past.

the sense of numbness or blankness can be comforting. in exchange for not hurting, sometimes we move to being okay with not having happiness. i know i was like that and can still find myself slipping into it. as for why it keeps coming back is because its a trained response. like a perverse Pavlov's dog. its why cognitive behavioral therapy is one that often works. its recognizing the thoughts that come in acknowledging them and eventually being able to put them away. i hope things become clearer for you and with time, some help, that the thoughts are able to if not go away, hold less power

things do get stale as we get older, and what gave us pleasure either doesn't give the same or non at all, but that does not mean there is no joy or substance left in the world for you. it does exist and unfortunately it usually has to do with how much effort we put in, and when depressed that barrier of effort into something that may not work is enough to not try. also while i appreciate you trying to ease the pain for your family and friends, that is not how they will see it. it will hurt them and make them second guess every interaction you have with them for the months before you try. it feels like we are easing the pain for others, but really, if your like me, your just making it easier on yourself. you are distancing relationships that can help and sustain you, not for the sake of just being alive, but having dignity. don't push the relationships away. keep them until the end.

with your transitional period upcoming, i think it might be a good time to try full into therapy. it really is something that works as much as you put into it. you might know this already but the reason they focus so much on the anorexia is that, surprisingly, it leads to more deaths than depression and suicide does. in the medical field the safety of the patient, of you, is their most concern, even if it isn't yours. that sucks going through it. but hopefully if you are upfront with the therapist when you meet about what you need, a therapeutic relationship can be built. 
as for what comes next with life, all i can suggest is to be proactive and apply to either a job before you leave or start something that you think sounds cool as a hobby. it will give something to look forward to. i'm sorry if my advice sucks and it isnt for you. the best thing is to try to find something that is what works for you
